## Factorization

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/index/03-concept; notes-page: factorization/index.qmd; note-sha256: 27a94d00e5bf4bd03de8cf88d25a71474442657b5c330d2911f33ad5d6e4d1ae; role: concept -->

One row in the course matrix is an inventory record selected within a Glottocode, not an unqualified language.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Moran and McCloy's PHOIBLE 2.0 release collects phonological inventory records contributed by many descriptive sources. The download and license page distributes the release as a CLDF StructureDataset under CC BY-SA 3.0. An inventory record generally describes a doculect, but multiple records may share a Glottocode and some source collections aggregate several varieties. Thus one row in the course matrix is an inventory record selected within a Glottocode, not an unqualified language.

The primary analysis centers without variance standardization because standardization would give relatively greater weight to rare listings.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Linguistic data matrices define the row, column, and cell units, reproduce the Glottocode-level row selection, and retain segment columns using training records only. Centering and scaling then compare two transformations of the empirical binary columns. Principal component analysis derives the covariance identity from the same decomposition and adds macroarea only after fitting for descriptive interpretation.

[Transcript]

Rank-one structure fits the first singular triplet and places the observed centered cells beside their rank-one reconstruction. Because families are not the split unit, the result does not establish transfer to unseen language families.

Reconstruction hides listed and not-listed cells in each held-out record, estimates scores from the remaining cells, and returns predictions to the original cell scale. The official MegaAcceptability archive is CC BY-SA 4.0; its internal README identifies the release as v1.2. ## From decomposition to supervised prediction

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/index/11-concept; notes-page: factorization/index.qmd; note-sha256: 27a94d00e5bf4bd03de8cf88d25a71474442657b5c330d2911f33ad5d6e4d1ae; role: concept -->

It does not treat automatically acquired counts as grammatical labels or test abstract linguistic representations in general.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The VALEX--MegaAcceptability page predicts MegaAcceptability profiles from VALEX subcategorization-frame proportions and compares the direct proportions with a PCA-compressed representation for verbs absent during fitting. Participant normalization, response aggregation, predictor centering, PCA, and tuning all occur inside their training splits. The application asks whether this shallow compression helps the held-out-verb target. It does not treat automatically acquired counts as grammatical labels or test abstract linguistic representations in general.

We will thus call one row an **inventory record**, not a language.

PHOIBLE 2.0 is a curated collection of phonological inventory records assembled from descriptive sources. The complete row for object $i$ is

$$
\mathbf x_i^{\mathsf T}

\mathbf x_{\cdot j}

\end{bmatrix}^{\mathsf T}.
$$

## Information retained by the matrix

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/data-matrices/13-concept; notes-page: factorization/data-matrices.qmd; note-sha256: 0d517c55addc1122510b29e7c6d76a9e9f2248c1fa881b984e83c33738b4a4c9; role: concept -->

Matrix methods cannot infer that an omitted distinction was theoretically intended, nor can they recover within-source detail removed before construction.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Changing a row from an inventory record to a Glottocode-level average would change the observational unit. Changing the columns would change which segment contrasts are available. Repeating a column would give the corresponding listing pattern extra numerical weight. Matrix methods cannot infer that an omitted distinction was theoretically intended, nor can they recover within-source detail removed before construction.

[Sources]

https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.2593234
https://phoible.github.io/faq/
https://phoible.org/download
:::

## Centering and scaling

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/centering-and-scaling/02-concept; notes-page: factorization/centering-and-scaling.qmd; note-sha256: 1b7626b262a8c30711660b23a2ace9a8faaa53901e1c992b484e958d65a25b81; role: concept -->

Standardization would additionally change its unit and, for binary data, its weight in the factorization.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The PHOIBLE matrix represents inventory records in rows and retained segment listings in columns. Every column uses the same binary database-listing unit, but the columns differ in how often a segment is listed. Centering changes each column's origin. Standardization would additionally change its unit and, for binary data, its weight in the factorization.

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/centering-and-scaling.qmd
:::

## Centering changes the origin {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/centering-and-scaling/03-math; notes-page: factorization/centering-and-scaling.qmd; note-sha256: 1b7626b262a8c30711660b23a2ace9a8faaa53901e1c992b484e958d65a25b81; role: math -->

For column $j$, the training mean is

$$
\widehat\mu_j
=
\frac{1}{n_{\mathcal T}}
\sum_{i\in\mathcal T}x_{ij}.
$$

Because $x_{ij}$ is binary here, $\widehat\mu_j$ is the training proportion of inventory records that list segment $j$.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

For column $j$, the training mean is

$$
\widehat\mu_j
=
\frac{1}{n_{\mathcal T}}
\sum_{i\in\mathcal T}x_{ij}.
$$

Because $x_{ij}$ is binary here, $\widehat\mu_j$ is the training proportion of inventory records that list segment $j$.

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/centering-and-scaling.qmd
:::

## Centering changes the origin {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/centering-and-scaling/04-math; notes-page: factorization/centering-and-scaling.qmd; note-sha256: 1b7626b262a8c30711660b23a2ace9a8faaa53901e1c992b484e958d65a25b81; role: math -->

The centered entry is

$$
z_{ij}=x_{ij}-\widehat\mu_j,
$$

and the complete centered training matrix is

$$
\mathbf Z_{\mathcal T}
=
\mathbf X_{\mathcal T}
-
\mathbf 1_{n_{\mathcal T}}\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}^{\mathsf T}.
$$

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The centered entry is

$$
z_{ij}=x_{ij}-\widehat\mu_j,
$$

and the complete centered training matrix is

$$
\mathbf Z_{\mathcal T}
=
\mathbf X_{\mathcal T}
-
\mathbf 1_{n_{\mathcal T}}\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}^{\mathsf T}.
$$

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/centering-and-scaling.qmd
:::

## Centering changes the origin

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/centering-and-scaling/05-concept; notes-page: factorization/centering-and-scaling.qmd; note-sha256: 1b7626b262a8c30711660b23a2ace9a8faaa53901e1c992b484e958d65a25b81; role: concept -->

It changes the reference point from “not listed” to the observed training prevalence.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Every column of $\mathbf Z_{\mathcal T}$ has mean zero. Centering does not alter differences between inventory records. It changes the reference point from “not listed” to the observed training prevalence.

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/centering-and-scaling.qmd
:::

## Scaling changes the unit {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/centering-and-scaling/06-math; notes-page: factorization/centering-and-scaling.qmd; note-sha256: 1b7626b262a8c30711660b23a2ace9a8faaa53901e1c992b484e958d65a25b81; role: math -->

The sample standard deviation of column $j$ is

$$
s_j
=
\sqrt{
\frac{1}{n_{\mathcal T}-1}
\sum_{i\in\mathcal T}
(x_{ij}-\widehat\mu_j)^2
}.
$$

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The sample standard deviation of column $j$ is

$$
s_j
=
\sqrt{
\frac{1}{n_{\mathcal T}-1}
\sum_{i\in\mathcal T}
(x_{ij}-\widehat\mu_j)^2
}.
$$

## Scaling changes the unit {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/centering-and-scaling/07-math; notes-page: factorization/centering-and-scaling.qmd; note-sha256: 1b7626b262a8c30711660b23a2ace9a8faaa53901e1c992b484e958d65a25b81; role: math -->

Collecting these values on the diagonal of $\mathbf S$, the standardized matrix is

$$
\widetilde{\mathbf Z}_{\mathcal T}
=
\mathbf Z_{\mathcal T}\mathbf S^{-1},
$$

or, cell by cell,

$$
\widetilde z_{ij}
=
\frac{x_{ij}-\widehat\mu_j}{s_j}.
$$

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Collecting these values on the diagonal of $\mathbf S$, the standardized matrix is

$$
\widetilde{\mathbf Z}_{\mathcal T}
=
\mathbf Z_{\mathcal T}\mathbf S^{-1},
$$

It gives every segment column the same variance before factorization.

## The empirical weighting decision

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/centering-and-scaling/12-concept; notes-page: factorization/centering-and-scaling.qmd; note-sha256: 1b7626b262a8c30711660b23a2ace9a8faaa53901e1c992b484e958d65a25b81; role: concept -->

That weighting may be useful for some questions, but it is not neutral.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The least variable retained column would be multiplied by 8.82, whereas the most variable would be multiplied by 2.01. Standardization would thus assign relatively greater weight to rare segment listings. That weighting may be useful for some questions, but it is not neutral.

[Sources]

:::

## The empirical weighting decision

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/centering-and-scaling/13-concept; notes-page: factorization/centering-and-scaling.qmd; note-sha256: 1b7626b262a8c30711660b23a2ace9a8faaa53901e1c992b484e958d65a25b81; role: concept -->

It defines the numerical target of this factorization.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The primary PHOIBLE analysis centers without variance standardization. Every column already shares the same listing unit, and the analysis lets common patterns contribute their observed variance. This choice does not claim that common segments are linguistically more important. It defines the numerical target of this factorization.

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/centering-and-scaling.qmd
:::

## Rank-one structure

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/rank-one-structure/02-concept; notes-page: factorization/rank-one-structure.qmd; note-sha256: 4a0f5b997e006e5ff823227006fe39bda4cce64e4aac496dde3d25c0ad21b61a; role: concept -->

A rank-one approximation asks what can be represented by one row pattern and one column pattern before adding further components.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The centered PHOIBLE inventory matrix contains many linked listing patterns. A rank-one approximation asks what can be represented by one row pattern and one column pattern before adding further components.

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/rank-one-structure.qmd
:::

## Constructing one outer product {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/rank-one-structure/03-math; notes-page: factorization/rank-one-structure.qmd; note-sha256: 4a0f5b997e006e5ff823227006fe39bda4cce64e4aac496dde3d25c0ad21b61a; role: math -->

For a matrix with $n$ rows and $p$ columns, let

$$
\mathbf a
=
\begin{bmatrix}
a_1&\cdots&a_n
\end{bmatrix}^{\mathsf T}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathbf b
=
\begin{bmatrix}
b_1&\cdots&b_p
\end{bmatrix}^{\mathsf T}.
$$

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

For a matrix with $n$ rows and $p$ columns, let

$$
\mathbf a
=
\begin{bmatrix}
a_1&\cdots&a_n
\end{bmatrix}^{\mathsf T}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathbf b
=
\begin{bmatrix}
b_1&\cdots&b_p
\end{bmatrix}^{\mathsf T}.
$$

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/rank-one-structure.qmd
:::

## Constructing one outer product {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/rank-one-structure/04-math; notes-page: factorization/rank-one-structure.qmd; note-sha256: 4a0f5b997e006e5ff823227006fe39bda4cce64e4aac496dde3d25c0ad21b61a; role: math -->

Their outer product is

$$
\mathbf a\mathbf b^{\mathsf T}
=
\begin{bmatrix}
a_1b_1&\cdots&a_1b_p\\
\vdots&\ddots&\vdots\\
a_nb_1&\cdots&a_nb_p
\end{bmatrix}.
$$

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Their outer product is

$$
\mathbf a\mathbf b^{\mathsf T}
=
\begin{bmatrix}
a_1b_1&\cdots&a_1b_p\\
\vdots&\ddots&\vdots\\
a_nb_1&\cdots&a_nb_p
\end{bmatrix}.
$$

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/rank-one-structure.qmd
:::

## Constructing one outer product {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/rank-one-structure/05-math; notes-page: factorization/rank-one-structure.qmd; note-sha256: 4a0f5b997e006e5ff823227006fe39bda4cce64e4aac496dde3d25c0ad21b61a; role: math -->

Every cell obeys the same rule,

$$
x_{ij}=a_i b_j.
$$

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Every cell obeys the same rule,

$$
x_{ij}=a_i b_j.
$$

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/rank-one-structure.qmd
:::

## Constructing one outer product

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/rank-one-structure/06-concept; notes-page: factorization/rank-one-structure.qmd; note-sha256: 4a0f5b997e006e5ff823227006fe39bda4cce64e4aac496dde3d25c0ad21b61a; role: concept -->

Any nonzero matrix with this form has rank one.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Thus all columns are scalar multiples of $\mathbf a$, and all rows are scalar multiples of $\mathbf b^{\mathsf T}$. Any nonzero matrix with this form has rank one.

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/rank-one-structure.qmd
:::

## Constructing one outer product {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/rank-one-structure/07-math; notes-page: factorization/rank-one-structure.qmd; note-sha256: 4a0f5b997e006e5ff823227006fe39bda4cce64e4aac496dde3d25c0ad21b61a; role: math -->

The individual vector scales are not identified by the product. For any nonzero constant $c$,

$$
(c\mathbf a)
\left(\frac{1}{c}\mathbf b\right)^{\mathsf T}
=
\mathbf a\mathbf b^{\mathsf T}.
$$

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The individual vector scales are not identified by the product. For any nonzero constant $c$,

$$
(c\mathbf a)
\left(\frac{1}{c}\mathbf b\right)^{\mathsf T}
=
\mathbf a\mathbf b^{\mathsf T}.
$$

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/rank-one-structure.qmd
:::

## Constructing one outer product {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/rank-one-structure/08-math; notes-page: factorization/rank-one-structure.qmd; note-sha256: 4a0f5b997e006e5ff823227006fe39bda4cce64e4aac496dde3d25c0ad21b61a; role: math -->

The singular value decomposition resolves this scale convention by using unit-length vectors and a separate nonnegative strength $d_1$:

$$
\widehat{\mathbf Z}^{(1)}
=
d_1\mathbf u_1\mathbf v_1^{\mathsf T},
\qquad
\mathbf u_1^{\mathsf T}\mathbf u_1
=
\mathbf v_1^{\mathsf T}\mathbf v_1
=1.
$$

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The singular value decomposition resolves this scale convention by using unit-length vectors and a separate nonnegative strength $d_1$:

$$
\widehat{\mathbf Z}^{(1)}
=
d_1\mathbf u_1\mathbf v_1^{\mathsf T},
\qquad
\mathbf u_1^{\mathsf T}\mathbf u_1
=
\mathbf v_1^{\mathsf T}\mathbf v_1
=1.
$$

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/rank-one-structure.qmd
:::

## Comparing observed and fitted cells

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/rank-one-structure/13-concept; notes-page: factorization/rank-one-structure.qmd; note-sha256: 4a0f5b997e006e5ff823227006fe39bda4cce64e4aac496dde3d25c0ad21b61a; role: concept -->

They are not probabilities.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The fitted panel is smoother because all its cells share one outer-product rule. Positive and negative values indicate deviations above and below training prevalence. They are not probabilities.

## Compression and interpretation {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/rank-one-structure/14-math; notes-page: factorization/rank-one-structure.qmd; note-sha256: 4a0f5b997e006e5ff823227006fe39bda4cce64e4aac496dde3d25c0ad21b61a; role: math -->

The reduction can be substantial, but it is useful only when the residual matrix

$$
\mathbf E^{(1)}
=
\mathbf Z-\widehat{\mathbf Z}^{(1)}
$$

is small enough for the target at hand.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

An unrestricted $n\times p$ matrix contains $np$ cells. A rank-one representation stores $n+p+1$ fitted quantities before accounting for the unit-length and sign conventions. The reduction can be substantial, but it is useful only when the residual matrix

$$
\mathbf E^{(1)}
=
\mathbf Z-\widehat{\mathbf Z}^{(1)}
$$

is small enough for the target at hand.

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/rank-one-structure.qmd
:::

Rank is an algebraic property before it is a linguistic hypothesis.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The component is a numerical direction. PHOIBLE family and macroarea metadata do not enter this fit, and a high loading does not by itself identify a phonological natural class. Rank is an algebraic property before it is a linguistic hypothesis.

## Singular value decomposition

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/singular-value-decomposition/02-concept; notes-page: factorization/singular-value-decomposition.qmd; note-sha256: 516c5e6b01cdeb279f944b9f82aa50c5312c0619eced93ed0984ebd4ead965f0; role: concept -->

The singular value decomposition (SVD) expresses that matrix as a sequence of mutually orthogonal rank-one terms, ordered by the centered sum of squares each term represents.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

One rank-one pattern leaves substantial structure in the centered PHOIBLE matrix. The singular value decomposition (SVD) expresses that matrix as a sequence of mutually orthogonal rank-one terms, ordered by the centered sum of squares each term represents.

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/singular-value-decomposition.qmd
:::

## Stating the reduced decomposition {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/singular-value-decomposition/03-math; notes-page: factorization/singular-value-decomposition.qmd; note-sha256: 516c5e6b01cdeb279f944b9f82aa50c5312c0619eced93ed0984ebd4ead965f0; role: math -->

For $\mathbf Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ with rank $r$, the reduced SVD is

$$
\mathbf Z
=
\mathbf U\mathbf D\mathbf V^{\mathsf T},
$$

where

$$
\mathbf U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r},
\qquad
\mathbf D\in\mathbb R^{r\times r},
\qquad
\mathbf V\in\mathbb R^{p\times r}.
$$

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

For $\mathbf Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ with rank $r$, the reduced SVD is

$$
\mathbf Z
=
\mathbf U\mathbf D\mathbf V^{\mathsf T},
$$

where

$$
\mathbf U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r},
\qquad
\mathbf D\in\mathbb R^{r\times r},
\qquad
\mathbf V\in\mathbb R^{p\times r}.
$$

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/singular-value-decomposition.qmd
:::

## Stating the reduced decomposition {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/singular-value-decomposition/04-math; notes-page: factorization/singular-value-decomposition.qmd; note-sha256: 516c5e6b01cdeb279f944b9f82aa50c5312c0619eced93ed0984ebd4ead965f0; role: math -->

The columns are orthonormal,

$$
\mathbf U^{\mathsf T}\mathbf U=\mathbf I_r,
\qquad
\mathbf V^{\mathsf T}\mathbf V=\mathbf I_r,
$$

and $\mathbf D$ is diagonal with ordered nonnegative entries,

$$
d_1\ge d_2\ge\cdots\ge d_r>0.
$$

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The columns are orthonormal,

$$
\mathbf U^{\mathsf T}\mathbf U=\mathbf I_r,
\qquad
\mathbf V^{\mathsf T}\mathbf V=\mathbf I_r,
$$

and $\mathbf D$ is diagonal with ordered nonnegative entries,

$$
d_1\ge d_2\ge\cdots\ge d_r>0.
$$

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/singular-value-decomposition.qmd
:::

## Stating the reduced decomposition

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/singular-value-decomposition/05-concept; notes-page: factorization/singular-value-decomposition.qmd; note-sha256: 516c5e6b01cdeb279f944b9f82aa50c5312c0619eced93ed0984ebd4ead965f0; role: concept -->

The vectors $\mathbf u_k$ locate the row objects along component $k$, the vectors $\mathbf v_k$ define the corresponding column directions, and $d_k$ gives the component's strength.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The vectors $\mathbf u_k$ locate the row objects along component $k$, the vectors $\mathbf v_k$ define the corresponding column directions, and $d_k$ gives the component's strength.

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/singular-value-decomposition.qmd
:::

## From a matrix product to rank-one terms {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/singular-value-decomposition/06-math; notes-page: factorization/singular-value-decomposition.qmd; note-sha256: 516c5e6b01cdeb279f944b9f82aa50c5312c0619eced93ed0984ebd4ead965f0; role: math -->

Multiplying by the diagonal matrix scales matched columns of $\mathbf U$ and $\mathbf V$. Thus

$$
\mathbf Z
=
\sum_{k=1}^{r}
d_k\mathbf u_k\mathbf v_k^{\mathsf T}.
$$

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Multiplying by the diagonal matrix scales matched columns of $\mathbf U$ and $\mathbf V$. Thus

$$
\mathbf Z
=
\sum_{k=1}^{r}
d_k\mathbf u_k\mathbf v_k^{\mathsf T}.
$$

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/singular-value-decomposition.qmd
:::

## From a matrix product to rank-one terms {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/singular-value-decomposition/07-math; notes-page: factorization/singular-value-decomposition.qmd; note-sha256: 516c5e6b01cdeb279f944b9f82aa50c5312c0619eced93ed0984ebd4ead965f0; role: math -->

Every summand is rank one. The rank-$K$ approximation keeps the first $K$ terms:

$$
\widehat{\mathbf Z}^{(K)}
=
\sum_{k=1}^{K}
d_k\mathbf u_k\mathbf v_k^{\mathsf T}
=
\mathbf U_K\mathbf D_K\mathbf V_K^{\mathsf T}.
$$

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Every summand is rank one. The rank-$K$ approximation keeps the first $K$ terms:

$$
\widehat{\mathbf Z}^{(K)}
=
\sum_{k=1}^{K}
d_k\mathbf u_k\mathbf v_k^{\mathsf T}
=
\mathbf U_K\mathbf D_K\mathbf V_K^{\mathsf T}.
$$

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/singular-value-decomposition.qmd
:::

## From a matrix product to rank-one terms {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/singular-value-decomposition/08-math; notes-page: factorization/singular-value-decomposition.qmd; note-sha256: 516c5e6b01cdeb279f944b9f82aa50c5312c0619eced93ed0984ebd4ead965f0; role: math -->

Among all rank-$K$ matrices, this approximation minimizes squared reconstruction error:

$$
\widehat{\mathbf Z}^{(K)}
=
\arg\min_{\operatorname{rank}(\mathbf A)\le K}
\|\mathbf Z-\mathbf A\|_F^2.
$$

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Among all rank-$K$ matrices, this approximation minimizes squared reconstruction error:

$$
\widehat{\mathbf Z}^{(K)}
=
\arg\min_{\operatorname{rank}(\mathbf A)\le K}
\|\mathbf Z-\mathbf A\|_F^2.
$$

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/singular-value-decomposition.qmd
:::

## From a matrix product to rank-one terms {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/singular-value-decomposition/09-math; notes-page: factorization/singular-value-decomposition.qmd; note-sha256: 516c5e6b01cdeb279f944b9f82aa50c5312c0619eced93ed0984ebd4ead965f0; role: math -->

The Frobenius norm is the sum of squared cells,

$$
\|\mathbf A\|_F^2
=
\sum_i\sum_j a_{ij}^2.
$$

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The Frobenius norm is the sum of squared cells,

$$
\|\mathbf A\|_F^2
=
\sum_i\sum_j a_{ij}^2.
$$

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/singular-value-decomposition.qmd
:::

## From a matrix product to rank-one terms {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/singular-value-decomposition/10-math; notes-page: factorization/singular-value-decomposition.qmd; note-sha256: 516c5e6b01cdeb279f944b9f82aa50c5312c0619eced93ed0984ebd4ead965f0; role: math -->

Orthogonality yields

$$
\|\mathbf Z\|_F^2
=
\sum_{k=1}^{r}d_k^2,
\qquad
\|\mathbf Z-\widehat{\mathbf Z}^{(K)}\|_F^2
=
\sum_{k=K+1}^{r}d_k^2.
$$

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Orthogonality yields

$$
\|\mathbf Z\|_F^2
=
\sum_{k=1}^{r}d_k^2,
\qquad
\|\mathbf Z-\widehat{\mathbf Z}^{(K)}\|_F^2
=
\sum_{k=K+1}^{r}d_k^2.
$$

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/singular-value-decomposition.qmd
:::

## Sign and directional limits

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/singular-value-decomposition/16-concept; notes-page: factorization/singular-value-decomposition.qmd; note-sha256: 516c5e6b01cdeb279f944b9f82aa50c5312c0619eced93ed0984ebd4ead965f0; role: concept -->

Interpretation should concern contrasts among loadings or scores, not a privileged positive orientation.

[Transcript]

## Sign and directional limits

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/singular-value-decomposition/17-concept; notes-page: factorization/singular-value-decomposition.qmd; note-sha256: 516c5e6b01cdeb279f944b9f82aa50c5312c0619eced93ed0984ebd4ead965f0; role: concept -->

This is a stronger limitation than sign indeterminacy.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

If singular values are equal or nearly equal, rotations within the corresponding subspace can also leave the fit unchanged or nearly unchanged. The subspace may then be more stable than any one plotted axis. This is a stronger limitation than sign indeterminacy.

[Sources]

## Principal component analysis

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/principal-component-analysis/02-concept; notes-page: factorization/principal-component-analysis.qmd; note-sha256: b22ad754760faeab1485ce21cc83f2a7a004f2712c1ca759f3fe53d6e5495ef6; role: concept -->

It does not use phonological labels, family names, or macroareas to fit the directions.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Principal component analysis (PCA) finds directions along which centered rows vary. For the PHOIBLE matrix, a row is an inventory record and a column is a segment listing. PCA thus summarizes covariance among database-segment columns. It does not use phonological labels, family names, or macroareas to fit the directions.

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/principal-component-analysis.qmd
:::

$$
\mathbf Z
=

-

$$
\mathbf t=\mathbf Z\mathbf v.

$$
\operatorname{Var}[\mathbf t]
=

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}

&=\frac{1}{n-1}\mathbf Z^{\mathsf T}\mathbf Z\\

\mathbf U\mathbf D\mathbf V^{\mathsf T}\\
&=\mathbf V
\frac{\mathbf D^2}{n-1}
\mathbf V^{\mathsf T}.
\end{aligned}
$$

## Interpreting the variance criterion narrowly

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/principal-component-analysis/17-concept; notes-page: factorization/principal-component-analysis.qmd; note-sha256: b22ad754760faeab1485ce21cc83f2a7a004f2712c1ca759f3fe53d6e5495ef6; role: concept -->

Those targets require an external criterion.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

PCA maximizes variance in the supplied representation. Here that representation contains centered binary listings for training-retained segments. A direction with high variance is not necessarily the best direction for reconstruction of hidden cells, classification, or a linguistic theory. Those targets require an external criterion.

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/principal-component-analysis.qmd
:::

## Scores and loadings

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/scores-and-loadings/02-concept; notes-page: factorization/scores-and-loadings.qmd; note-sha256: 5f5becbc9ae67bbd8bfbbb61cd9372b80a5480be5900c4c959d33ac0f7afbfcf; role: concept -->

Keeping these index sets separate prevents a segment contrast from being described as if it were an inventory property.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The PHOIBLE decomposition produces two related objects with different units. Scores locate inventory records in the fitted component coordinates. Loadings describe directions across segment columns. ## Reconstruction

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/reconstruction/02-concept; notes-page: factorization/reconstruction.qmd; note-sha256: 2a267fe25e83d6bde3b7a78f0a05e73cda0c87501a88c0b4a4ee5ad7f50a2637; role: concept -->

We evaluate that reconstruction with a matrix-completion task.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Scores and loadings rebuild a matrix cell by cell. We evaluate that reconstruction with a matrix-completion task: learn segment structure from training inventories, choose rank with validation inventories, and reconstruct six cells hidden from each test inventory while its other retained segment cells remain visible.

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/reconstruction.qmd
:::

## Reconstructing with the first $K$ terms {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/reconstruction/06-math; notes-page: factorization/reconstruction.qmd; note-sha256: 2a267fe25e83d6bde3b7a78f0a05e73cda0c87501a88c0b4a4ee5ad7f50a2637; role: math -->

For an observed training matrix, the residual is

$$
\mathbf E^{(K)}
=
\mathbf Z-\widehat{\mathbf Z}^{(K)},
$$

and the fraction of centered sum of squares represented is

$$
R_K
=
\frac{\sum_{k=1}^{K}d_k^2}
     {\sum_{k=1}^{r}d_k^2}
=
1-
\frac{\|\mathbf E^{(K)}\|_F^2}
     {\|\mathbf Z\|_F^2}.
$$

## Reconstructing partially observed inventories {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/reconstruction/08-math; notes-page: factorization/reconstruction.qmd; note-sha256: 2a267fe25e83d6bde3b7a78f0a05e73cda0c87501a88c0b4a4ee5ad7f50a2637; role: math -->

$$

## What reconstruction establishes

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/reconstruction/16-concept; notes-page: factorization/reconstruction.qmd; note-sha256: 2a267fe25e83d6bde3b7a78f0a05e73cda0c87501a88c0b4a4ee5ad7f50a2637; role: concept -->

It does not reconstruct a wholly unseen inventory, establish phonological absence from a zero, or show that rank 40 is a phonological universal.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The result supports a narrow conclusion: structure learned from training inventory records helps complete a few hidden database listings when most of a held-out record is observed. It does not reconstruct a wholly unseen inventory, establish phonological absence from a zero, or show that rank 40 is a phonological universal.

[Sources]

The matrix-completion evaluation thus separates three operations: fit directions on training inventories, choose rank on validation inventories, and estimate performance once on test inventories.

## Separating fitting, selection, and evaluation {.compact}

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/choosing-components/03-list; notes-page: factorization/choosing-components.qmd; note-sha256: d1b31c1f54d263c100d0b2ae2f2cbe376199b51675b05c04e15908e516ed5a94; role: list -->

Let $\mathcal T$, $\mathcal V$, and $\mathcal E$ denote training, validation, and test inventory records. Training data determine:

1. Which segment columns occur often enough to retain;
2. The segment means $\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}_{\mathcal T}$;
3. The component directions $\mathbf V_{\mathcal T}$.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Let $\mathcal T$, $\mathcal V$, and $\mathcal E$ denote training, validation, and test inventory records. Training data determine: which segment columns occur often enough to retain. the segment means $\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}_{\mathcal T}$. the component directions $\mathbf V_{\mathcal T}$.

## Separating fitting, selection, and evaluation {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/choosing-components/04-math; notes-page: factorization/choosing-components.qmd; note-sha256: d1b31c1f54d263c100d0b2ae2f2cbe376199b51675b05c04e15908e516ed5a94; role: math -->

For a validation inventory with masked cells, scores at rank $K$ are

$$
\widehat{\mathbf t}_{i,K}
=
(\mathbf x_i^*-\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}_{\mathcal T})^{\mathsf T}
\mathbf V_{\mathcal T,K},
$$

and the reconstruction is

$$
\widehat{\mathbf x}_{i,K}
=
\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}_{\mathcal T}
+
\mathbf V_{\mathcal T,K}\widehat{\mathbf t}_{i,K}.
$$

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

For a validation inventory with masked cells, scores at rank $K$ are

$$
\widehat{\mathbf t}_{i,K}
=
(\mathbf x_i^*-\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}_{\mathcal T})^{\mathsf T}
\mathbf V_{\mathcal T,K},
$$

and the reconstruction is

$$
\widehat{\mathbf x}_{i,K}
=
\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}_{\mathcal T}
+
\mathbf V_{\mathcal T,K}\widehat{\mathbf t}_{i,K}.
$$

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/choosing-components.qmd
:::

## Separating fitting, selection, and evaluation {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/choosing-components/05-math; notes-page: factorization/choosing-components.qmd; note-sha256: d1b31c1f54d263c100d0b2ae2f2cbe376199b51675b05c04e15908e516ed5a94; role: math -->

The selected rank is

$$
\widehat K
=
\arg\min_{K\in\mathcal K}
L_{\mathrm{bal}}(\mathcal V,K),
$$

where

$$
L_{\mathrm{bal}}
=
\frac{1}{2n_1}\sum_{x=1}(x-\widehat x)^2
+
\frac{1}{2n_0}\sum_{x=0}(x-\widehat x)^2.
$$

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The selected rank is

$$
\widehat K
=
\arg\min_{K\in\mathcal K}
L_{\mathrm{bal}}(\mathcal V,K),
$$

where

$$
L_{\mathrm{bal}}
=
\frac{1}{2n_1}\sum_{x=1}(x-\widehat x)^2
+
\frac{1}{2n_0}\sum_{x=0}(x-\widehat x)^2.
$$

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/choosing-components.qmd
:::

## Separating fitting, selection, and evaluation

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/choosing-components/06-concept; notes-page: factorization/choosing-components.qmd; note-sha256: d1b31c1f54d263c100d0b2ae2f2cbe376199b51675b05c04e15908e516ed5a94; role: concept -->

Otherwise the test set becomes another validation set, the one-split repeated-decisions problem.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The final test loss is evaluated at $\widehat K$. Test loss must not be used to revise $\mathcal K$, preprocessing, or the masking procedure. Otherwise the test set becomes another validation set, the one-split repeated-decisions problem.

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/choosing-components.qmd
:::

## Preserving one final evaluation

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/choosing-components/11-concept; notes-page: factorization/choosing-components.qmd; note-sha256: d1b31c1f54d263c100d0b2ae2f2cbe376199b51675b05c04e15908e516ed5a94; role: concept -->

::: {.notes}

One inventory was sampled per Glottocode, and the split is stratified by macroarea. Families were not assigned wholesale to splits. Thus this evaluation concerns held-out inventory records under broad area balance; it does not establish transfer to unseen families.

## Why other criteria answer different questions

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/choosing-components/12-concept; notes-page: factorization/choosing-components.qmd; note-sha256: d1b31c1f54d263c100d0b2ae2f2cbe376199b51675b05c04e15908e516ed5a94; role: concept -->

It does not identify a true number of phonological dimensions.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Choosing a rank from observed training reconstruction rewards additional components by construction. A scree bend or a cumulative-variance threshold may summarize the observed matrix, but neither directly evaluates hidden cells. Conversely, validation loss is tied to the masking rule, loss function, and new-inventory target. It does not identify a true number of phonological dimensions.

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/choosing-components.qmd
:::

## Why other criteria answer different questions

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/choosing-components/13-concept; notes-page: factorization/choosing-components.qmd; note-sha256: d1b31c1f54d263c100d0b2ae2f2cbe376199b51675b05c04e15908e516ed5a94; role: concept -->

Letting validation or test inventories determine retained columns would create leakage through preprocessing.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Rank selection also includes preprocessing. Segment retention, centering, component fitting, and masking must remain inside their assigned partitions. Letting validation or test inventories determine retained columns would create leakage through preprocessing.

[Sources]

Course note: factorization/choosing-components.qmd
:::

The counts may contain parsing and frame-assignment error, and the release does not disambiguate verb senses.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

VALEX was acquired automatically from five corpora and the Web. Korhonen, Krymolowski, and Briscoe's dataset paper describes counts for English verb subcategorization frames and emphasizes automatic acquisition. The counts may contain parsing and frame-assignment error, and the release does not disambiguate verb senses.

## From VALEX distributions to MegaAcceptability profiles

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/valex-megaacceptability/05-concept; notes-page: factorization/valex-megaacceptability.qmd; note-sha256: d8a6442e85783bde67de49a7c12f4b985969880c942aa270c24cdb0ffc0a0d31; role: concept -->

The teaching analysis uses their empirical target but simplifies the model so that PCA is the only representational change.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The official MegaAcceptability archive is CC BY-SA 4.0, and its internal README identifies the release as v1.2. It contains judgments for English clause-embedding verbs in semantically bleached frames. White and Rawlins (2020) constructed lists in which each verb and frame appeared at most once, collected ordinal responses from participants reporting native American English, and modeled the relation between corpus frequencies and acceptability. The teaching analysis uses their empirical target but simplifies the model so that PCA is the only representational change.

[Sources]

=
\frac{c_{vj}}{\sum_h c_{vh}}.

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/valex-megaacceptability/08-math; notes-page: factorization/valex-megaacceptability.qmd; note-sha256: d8a6442e85783bde67de49a7c12f4b985969880c942aa270c24cdb0ffc0a0d31; role: math -->

The raw MegaAcceptability unit is one participant's ordinal response to one verb-frame item. Within a training set $\mathcal T$, participant $q$'s response is transformed as

z_{qi}
=

     {s_{q,\mathcal T}}.
$$

## Stating the competing procedures {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/valex-megaacceptability/12-math; notes-page: factorization/valex-megaacceptability.qmd; note-sha256: d8a6442e85783bde67de49a7c12f4b985969880c942aa270c24cdb0ffc0a0d31; role: math -->

The direct multivariate ridge model uses the complete VALEX proportion matrix. With an unpenalized intercept implemented by training centering, it solves

$$
(\widehat{\boldsymbol\beta}_{0,\lambda},
 \widehat{\mathbf B}_{\lambda})
=
\arg\min_{\boldsymbol\beta_0,\mathbf B}
\left\|\mathbf Y_{\mathcal T}
-\mathbf 1\boldsymbol\beta_0^{\mathsf T}
-\mathbf P_{\mathcal T}\mathbf B\right\|_F^2
+\lambda\|\mathbf B\|_F^2.
$$

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The direct multivariate ridge model uses the complete VALEX proportion matrix. With an unpenalized intercept implemented by training centering, it solves

$$
(\widehat{\boldsymbol\beta}_{0,\lambda},
 \widehat{\mathbf B}_{\lambda})
=
\arg\min_{\boldsymbol\beta_0,\mathbf B}
\left\|\mathbf Y_{\mathcal T}
-\mathbf 1\boldsymbol\beta_0^{\mathsf T}
-\mathbf P_{\mathcal T}\mathbf B\right\|_F^2
+\lambda\|\mathbf B\|_F^2.
$$

[Sources]

https://ilexir.co.uk/valex/
https://www.cs.brandeis.edu/~marc/misc/proceedings/lrec-2006/pdf/558_pdf.pdf
https://megaattitude.io/projects/mega-acceptability/mega-acceptability-v1.zip
https://doi.org/10.5334/gjgl.1001
:::

## Stating the competing procedures {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/valex-megaacceptability/13-math; notes-page: factorization/valex-megaacceptability.qmd; note-sha256: d8a6442e85783bde67de49a7c12f4b985969880c942aa270c24cdb0ffc0a0d31; role: math -->

The factor procedure fits PCA only to training predictor rows,

$$
\mathbf F_K
=
(\mathbf P-\mathbf 1\bar{\mathbf p}_{\mathcal T}^{\mathsf T})
\mathbf V_{\mathcal T,K},
$$

then substitutes $\mathbf F_K$ for $\mathbf P$ in the same ridge objective.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The factor procedure fits PCA only to training predictor rows,

$$
\mathbf F_K
=
(\mathbf P-\mathbf 1\bar{\mathbf p}_{\mathcal T}^{\mathsf T})
\mathbf V_{\mathcal T,K},
$$

then substitutes $\mathbf F_K$ for $\mathbf P$ in the same ridge objective.

## Keeping every fitted choice inside training data

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/valex-megaacceptability/16-concept; notes-page: factorization/valex-megaacceptability.qmd; note-sha256: d8a6442e85783bde67de49a7c12f4b985969880c942aa270c24cdb0ffc0a0d31; role: concept -->

Participant normalization, response aggregation, predictor centering, PCA loadings, rank, and penalty are refitted in the relevant training split.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Five repetitions of ten-fold outer cross-validation hold out complete verbs. Within every outer training set, independent five-fold validation selects the direct ridge penalty and jointly selects factor rank and ridge penalty. Participant normalization, response aggregation, predictor centering, PCA loadings, rank, and penalty are refitted in the relevant training split.

## Locating the predictive limitation

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/valex-megaacceptability/31-concept; notes-page: factorization/valex-megaacceptability.qmd; note-sha256: d8a6442e85783bde67de49a7c12f4b985969880c942aa270c24cdb0ffc0a0d31; role: concept -->

The present residual is consistent with that proposal, though it cannot separate communicativity from animacy, discourse, polysemy, item construction, or corpus-analysis error.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

White and Rawlins connect the object pattern to communicativity: with a verb such as *persuade*, the object may denote a recipient of communicated content. The present residual is consistent with that proposal, though it cannot separate communicativity from animacy, discourse, polysemy, item construction, or corpus-analysis error.

[Sources]

https://ilexir.co.uk/valex/
https://www.cs.brandeis.edu/~marc/misc/proceedings/lrec-2006/pdf/558_pdf.pdf

:::

## What the application establishes

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/valex-megaacceptability/32-concept; notes-page: factorization/valex-megaacceptability.qmd; note-sha256: d8a6442e85783bde67de49a7c12f4b985969880c942aa270c24cdb0ffc0a0d31; role: concept -->

The result counts against this shallow compression for this target, not against abstract syntactic or semantic representations in general.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

First, automatically acquired VALEX distributions contain information about MegaAcceptability profiles for verbs excluded from fitting. Second, PCA compression does not improve that mapping: the selected factor procedure performs slightly and stably worse than the direct profile. The result counts against this shallow compression for this target, not against abstract syntactic or semantic representations in general.

[Sources]

https://ilexir.co.uk/valex/
https://www.cs.brandeis.edu/~marc/misc/proceedings/lrec-2006/pdf/558_pdf.pdf
https://megaattitude.io/projects/mega-acceptability/mega-acceptability-v1.zip
https://doi.org/10.5334/gjgl.1001
:::

## What the application establishes

<!-- generated-slide-id: factorization/valex-megaacceptability/33-concept; notes-page: factorization/valex-megaacceptability.qmd; note-sha256: d8a6442e85783bde67de49a7c12f4b985969880c942aa270c24cdb0ffc0a0d31; role: concept -->

Those changes isolate the matrix operations taught here while preserving the held-out-verb question.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The teaching analysis differs from the paper in three declared ways. It uses raw VALEX proportions rather than the paper's best Beta Negative Binomial representation, PCA rather than a logistic factor model, and a fold-fitted z transformation rather than the released ordinal mixed-effects normalization. Those changes isolate the matrix operations taught here while preserving the held-out-verb question.

[Sources]

https://ilexir.co.uk/valex/
https://www.cs.brandeis.edu/~marc/misc/proceedings/lrec-2006/pdf/558_pdf.pdf

https://doi.org/10.5334/gjgl.1001
:::
